COFINFAD Analytics
Customer Lifecycle & Transactional Behavior Analysis for Colombian Fintech
Ji Guofang  •  Lin Yan  •  Nguyen Trong Nhan   |   Team 13  •  April 2026



COFINFAD
Visual Analytics Platform















Motivation & Objectives
Colombia's fintech sector is growing rapidly, yet many institutions lack accessible tools to analyze customer behavior and predict churn. This project aims to:

Democratize analytics — enable non-technical stakeholders to explore customer data through interactive visualizations
Identify behavioral segments — uncover distinct customer groups via unsupervised clustering on transactional features
Predict churn risk — build interpretable models that quantify churn probability and surface key drivers
Enable what-if analysis — let decision-makers simulate interventions and assess impact on retention


CORE QUESTION
"How can interactive visual analytics help Colombian fintech institutions understand, segment, and retain their customers?"

Methodology & Approach
We follow a 5-stage analytical framework that progresses from exploration to actionable simulation:



1
EXPLORE
— EDA with interactive charts & maps



2
CONFIRM
— Hypothesis testing via ggstatsplot



3
SEGMENT
— K-Means, Hierarchical, PAM clustering



4
CALIBRATE
— Lasso logistic regression for churn



5
SIMULATE
— What-if analysis with real-time sliders

Interactive Shiny Application — 5 Analytical Modules
All modules are integrated into a single dark-themed R Shiny dashboard at guofang1028.shinyapps.io/ShinyApp





MODULE 1
Exploratory Data Analysis
Interactive time-series charts, leaflet choropleth maps of regional distribution, and distribution plots by income bracket and transaction type.





Monthly Transaction Volume






MODULE 2
Confirmatory Analysis
Statistical hypothesis testing with ggbetweenstats (t-test, Welch, Mann-Whitney, Kruskal-Wallis) and correlation matrices.

MODULE 3
Customer Clustering
Multi-algorithm segmentation (K-Means, Hierarchical, PAM) with PCA scatter plots, silhouette validation, and heatmaps.

MODULE 4
Churn Prediction
Lasso (L1) logistic regression with cross-validation, variable importance ranking, and residual diagnostics.

MODULE 5
What-If Simulator
Interactive sliders to adjust customer attributes and observe real-time churn probability changes with sensitivity analysis.

Key Findings



Seasonal patterns differ by transaction type — Transfers peak mid-year while deposits show end-of-year spikes, confirmed by Kruskal-Wallis tests (p < 0.001).




Income brackets drive behavioral divergence — High-income customers average 3.2x more transaction volume than low-income segments, with significantly different product usage profiles.




Geographic clustering of churn risk — Rural departments show 40% higher churn probability than urban centers like Bogotá and Medellín, linked to limited product access.




Satisfaction score is the #1 churn predictor — Lasso feature selection consistently ranks satisfaction_score as the strongest predictor, followed by customer_tenure and active_products.




Product bundling reduces churn ~15% — What-if simulations show increasing active_products from 1 to 3 cuts predicted churn probability from ~47% to ~32%.





Discovered Customer Segments
Optimal clustering (k=4) reveals four distinct behavioral profiles across 10 engineered features:





Power Users
~18% of customers

High frequency, high value, long tenure. Low churn risk. Cross-sell opportunities.




Regular Users
~35% of customers

Consistent activity, moderate values. Stable segment. Upsell potential via engagement.




Occasional Users
~28% of customers

Sporadic engagement, low product count. Respond well to targeted campaigns.




At-Risk / New Adopters
~19% of customers

Very low activity, short tenure, high churn probability. Priority for onboarding programs.

Conclusion & Recommendations
COFINFAD Analytics demonstrates that interactive visual analytics can transform raw fintech data into actionable business intelligence. Our key recommendations:



1
Retain power users — Deploy loyalty programs with real-time satisfaction monitoring dashboards


2
Intervene on at-risk segments — Personalized outreach and product bundling within 90-day onboarding


3
Expand underserved regions — Region-specific campaigns for rural Colombian departments with high churn


4
Leverage what-if simulations — Use the simulator to quantify ROI of retention initiatives before deployment



Future Work

Integrate additional data sources (e.g., RFM scoring, external economic indicators)
Develop methods to proactively identify network effects among customer clusters
Expand the prediction module with ensemble models (Random Forest, XGBoost)
Add real-time data streaming for live dashboard monitoring
Incorporate NLP analysis on support ticket text for deeper churn driver insights
